title: Private VPC: graceful-degradation + local artifact validation PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments to safely perform control-plane upgrades and operator actions when customers are in minimal-egress or offline modes. Introduces a deterministic local artifact validation flow and a short, auditable egress grace period for emergency fetches. Also defines graceful-degradation behaviors for inference when remote dependencies are unavailable.
scope: This PRD covers: (1) on-host/local artifact validation (signed content-addressable mirrors), (2) conditional short-lived egress windows for approved operator actions, (3) deterministic upgrade rollback triggers when validation fails, and (4) runtime graceful-degradation modes (cached KV-only, quantized-fallback models, CPU-fallback with reduced QPS). Excludes UI work for console onboarding (handled by a separate ticket) and dedicated SaaS billing integration.
requirements: R1: Support a local artifact validation mode where operator/images/manifests are verified against signed metadata before install — includes signature chain, manifest hash and timestamp checks.

R2: Provide a configurable egress grace period (default 6 hours) that permits outbound fetches to approved mirror endpoints when operator requests explicit customer consent. Grace period must be auditable and reversible by the customer within the window.
R3: Implement an offline-first bootstrap flow: node verifies artifacts from local mirror or contiguous USB/imported bundle when no egress allowed.
R4: Define clear deterministic upgrade acceptance gates: checksum & signature verification, node-level resource checks (disk, memory), and health probe pass; otherwise auto-rollback.
R5: Telemetry shard: record only minimal operational telemetry for upgrade validation (hashes checked, signature status, timestamps) and respect telemetry redaction policy for PII-sensitive fields.

R6: Graceful-degradation modes: (a) KV-only reads for repeated prefixes using cached KV state; (b) fallback to quantized small-model variant when model snapshot unavailable; (c) accept throttled QPS and degraded latency SLAs during fallback.
R7: Customer-configurable allowlist of mirror endpoints and PKI roots; operator actions requiring egress must be validated against allowlist and customer-signed consent token.
R8: Provide simple operator UX signals in logs and audit: 'validation:passed|failed', 'egress:opened|closed', 'rollback:triggered', with correlating request IDs.

R9: KMS rotation and secrets handling: support deferred KMS key rotation window tied to upgrade windows; if rotation occurs mid-upgrade the operator must be able to revalidate artifacts with previous key using a signed key-rotation proof.
R10: Acceptance tests must run in three modes: full-egress, allowlisted-egress, and offline-import; all must pass to mark release candidate accepted for private deploys.

R11: Backward compatibility: nodes running runtime-1.x should be able to validate artifacts produced by runtime-1.(x+1) using documented compatibility rules; runtime will reject upgrades that require non-backward-compatible kernel switches unless explicit opt-in flag is set.

R12: Minimal-operator footprint: local validation should not require additional privileged network daemons beyond the existing operator image; any new privileged component must be justified and minimize attack surface.

R13: Rollback SLA: if validation failure detected after image activation, automated rollback must begin within 2 minutes and complete within 20 minutes for single-zone clusters (documented contingency for multi-zone).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A private cluster with 'offline' network profile can perform a mock upgrade using a provided signed artifact bundle (no egress) and pass all validation checks end-to-end.

AC2: A private cluster in 'allowlist' mode can open a 6-hour egress grace window via a customer-signed consent token, fetch missing artifacts from an allowlisted mirror, and record an immutable audit entry containing token id, operator id and timestamps.

AC3: If any artifact checksum or signature fails during pre-install validation, the upgrade is rejected and an automatic rollback plan is generated and stored in the cluster's upgrade history; telemetry shows 'validation:failed' with failure reason.

AC4: During a simulated global mirror outage, nodes automatically enter graceful-degradation mode: (a) serve cached prefixes from KV, (b) switch model routing to quantized fallback variant, and (c) reduce accepted QPS by configured throttle percent. All three behaviors must be observable and configurable via cluster config.

AC5: KMS rotation proof flow validated: a test where a key rotates during an upgrade must allow operator to re-validate artifacts using rotation-proof metadata; if revalidation fails, rollback must be triggered.

AC6: End-to-end tests included in the release pipeline: for each release candidate at least one full-e2e private deploy test must pass in each of the three network profiles (full, allowlist, offline).

AC7: Audit/log format verified: each upgrade event has a correlating audit record with fields: event_id, actor, network_profile, artifacts_checked (list of file hashes), validation_result, egress_window_id (if used).
decisions: D1: Default egress grace period set to 6 hours; customers may configure 0-72 hours per tenancy. Short default chosen to limit blast radius and match support SLA.
D2: Use content-addressable signed manifests (CAS+detached sig) for local validation instead of full OCI trust v2 to reduce operator surface and speed local checks.
D3: Graceful-degradation behavior will be opt-out for enterprise tiers on Dedicated but opt-in-by-default for Private to avoid surprising performance regressions.
D4: Telemetry will be minimal and limited to hashes and status; no raw artifacts or customer data may leave private clusters unless explicit customer consent is recorded.
open_questions: Q1: Should we allow operator-initiated on-demand revalidation of previously-accepted artifacts after a KMS rotation without rolling back?
Q2: What is the exact set of fields required in the customer's consent token to meet enterprise legal/compliance in EMEA customers?
Q3: Is a hardware-backed attestation (TPM) required for ATO customers to accept local artifact validation without egress?
Q4: How should we display grace-period usage in the Console audit UI (single line entry vs expanded timeline)?
